## anu-p07 — argument map

Of things (bhāvānām) no arising (na samudbhavaḥ) is — natural (sahajaḥ), by your contemplation (tvadbhāvitā) they shine (bhānti). Non-true (niḥsatyāḥ) too (api), truth (satyatām) they partake (bhajanti) by experience-delusion (anubhavabhrāntyā) for a moment (kṣaṇam). This universe-glory (eṣa viśvamahimā) will-born from you (tvatsaṅkalpajaḥ); its birth (janma) from elsewhere (anyataḥ) is not (nāsti). Hence (tasmāt) you shine (bhāsi) by splendor (vibhavena) in worlds (bhuvaneṣu) — one (ekaḥ), though (api), many-selfed (anekātmakaḥ).

### Open
- Whether 'sahaja' means 'natural' or 'innate' is unresolved.
- Whether 'anubhavabhrānti' means experience's delusion or delusion of experience is unresolved.
- Whether 'ekopy anekātmakaḥ' means 'one, though many-selfed' or 'one, yet (becoming) many-selfed' is unresolved.
